hook: SCP-5309 talks to you directly from its first line. A synthetic guide from the Pataphysics Department greets you as the reader, admits its job is to help you ignore the file, and then helps you read it anyway. Go in knowing that you are part of the setup, and that the article cares a great deal about what you choose to imagine while reading.
whyItMatters:
The file belongs to the strand of SCP writing that treats the Foundation as characters in a story and asks what follows from that. Its particular angle is small and unsettling: anything a reader never pictures, like a character's hair color or the leaves on a tree, may simply not be there.

What keeps it from being a pure thought experiment is a human core. The central figure is a researcher who comes back from beyond the page and finds that understanding her situation mostly makes her lonely.
thingsToNotice:
Track how the forest-and-trees idea grows: Berkeley returns from the jump unable to name her own hair color, decides that details nobody notices do not exist, and then, isolated, starts writing an imagined Tommy in her head and wonders whether she loves him or the idea of him. Her therapist's suggestion to talk to herself through writing quietly sets up the ending, and the disruption log shows staff losing memories and one researcher reporting that nothing outside his site exists, while Smalls hopes the readers never think to doubt them.

The last log puts Berkeley face to face with the lonely author, who confirms that her own written thoughts spread the idea that nothing exists and caused the collapse. She uses the imagined Tommy to pull her back, dies again on purpose, and is uploaded into the database by Enkidu. Sisyphus.sic, the friendly guide from the opening, turns out to be Berkeley herself, and her closing words leave the outcome in your hands.
